To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NusA interacts with an unfolded region in the amino-terminal domain of N that remains unstructured when N binds to the RNA boxB.

the N protein of bacteriphage lambda undergoes a structural transition when it binds to boxB, that this change is localized to the amino-terminal 30 amino acids of N, that this region remains disordered even when the full-length N protein binds to boxB and that the interaction of the N-box-B complex with the E. coli NusA antitermination factor is independent of RNA.

1) the binding of N to boxB RNA induces a significant structural change within the amino-terminal domain of the N protein, 2) NusA binds specifically to this unfolded domain of N, independent of the RNA, and 3) the C terminus, including the regions that are important for RNAP activation, remain unfolded when N binds to RNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how RNA polymerase (Pol II) transcription is regulated in eukaryotes.
the mechanism by which N protein, a small protein that binds to the nascent RNA of the lambda phage, activates RNA polymerase to overcome termination signals.
the assembly of the N-dependent transcription antitermination complex, which is a model for the assembly of a large multi-protein complex in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the N protein of lambda undergoes a series of structural transitions upon binding to its various partners within the N antitermination complex, and that each of these structural transitions is independent of the others.
the N-dependent antiternation complex of phage λ can be described as a complex of unfolded domains that are brought together by the specific interaction of RNA with the N protein.
the interaction of the N protein with NusA and with RNAP is independent of RNA, and that the interaction of RNA with the N protein is independent of the NusA and RNAP binding sites.

the NusA protein binds to an unfolded domain of the N protein, even though N is a multi-domain protein that is partially folded when bound to boxB RNA.
NusA interacts with a specific unfolded domain in N, and that NusA does so without any assistance from the RNA.
